solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nearly all titled women entertaining wealthy American spy

indicators.note: nearly all of a word stops just short of its end, so the last letter of the word all is dropped
entertaining guests means holding them inside, so the women's title goes round the money word

parts.note: dames are women holding a title, as in Dame Judi Dench
wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: A list of aristocratic ladies playing host to a rich American who turns out to be a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldrich Ames was a CIA officer who sold secrets to the Soviet Union; 'titled women' are DAMES, as in Dame Judi Dench.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldrich Ames is a real CIA officer convicted in 1994 of selling secrets to Moscow, so an example of a spy from the USA.

clue.text: Sharpness of spy I rate poorly

indicators.note: letters arranged poorly are put in a bad order, so the words before are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone rates a spy's keen wit only modestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is harshness or sharpness of tone or manner, a close synonym.

clue.text: Circle makes money getting rid of American spies

parts.note: a disc is a flat circle

indicators.note: getting rid of something means taking it out, so a letter is removed from the money word

parts.note: to make money is to earn it, here in the third person

explanation.surface: A ring of operatives turns a profit by expelling its American spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spies' looks like a plural noun but is the verb: she spies, she discerns.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to make out or perceive something, just as one spies it in the distance.

clue.text: Paper mannequin, diamond rings

indicators.note: the clue words ring, or surround, the letters wanted, which sit inside them across the word break

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a shop dummy wearing diamond rings.
explanation.walkthrough: India paper is very thin paper used for printing Bibles and dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: India paper is a thin opaque printing paper, so the place name stands for a kind of paper.

clue.text: More pleased with software that's installed inside an hour

indicators.note: something installed inside goes within, so these pieces are put inside the hour abbreviation

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour
an app is a piece of software
i.e., from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone is more content now their software is installed within the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Happier is the comparative of happy, meaning more contented or pleased.

clue.text: Give wrong title for Judi Dench as head spy

definitions.text: Give wrong title for Judi Dench as head spy

parts.words: Give wrong title for Judi Dench as head spy
parts.note: Judi Dench played M, the head of the secret service, in the Bond films

explanation.surface: Someone addresses Judi Dench incorrectly when she plays the spymaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as MISTER M: the male title wrongly given to Dench's M. To misterm is to name something wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: To misterm is to call something by the wrong name, which is giving a wrong title.

clue.text: We hear of someone cultivating greed — maybe just a little bit

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the phrase is said out loud to give the answer's sound

parts.note: greed is one of the deadly sins (hence 'maybe'), and someone cultivating soil is a tiller, so a sin tiller

explanation.surface: A remark that a person nurturing greed might be only slightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks greed as just one example of a sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or spark of something, a very small amount.

clue.text: Meal without a drink

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken off the meal

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
per means a, as in so much a head

explanation.surface: An evening meal served with nothing to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meal' wants to be the definition, and SUP can mean a meal, but the definition is 'drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to drink, especially in small mouthfuls.

clue.text: Emoticon spy

definitions.meaning: a face drawn in keyboard symbols, typically a grin
George ..., John le Carré's fictional intelligence officer

explanation.surface: A text symbol that might be used by an agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiling face icon is called by this name, and George Smiley is le Carré's spymaster hero.

clue.text: Books covering over vegetable

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the pieces are read backwards in this down entry

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books
atop means on top of, covering

explanation.surface: Books spread over the top of a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The potato is a starchy tuber eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Sat and thought, erasing previous answer

indicators.note: erasing something removes it, so those letters are struck out of the word for thought

parts.note: supposed means thought or believed
the answer to 7 across, the clue printed just before this one

explanation.surface: Someone sat and pondered, then rubbed out the answer they gave before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat' looks like sitting down; here it is sitting for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: A model who sat for a portrait posed for it.

clue.text: One has little hope for "Spies" — terrible film

indicators.note: something terrible is badly made, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as of condensation

explanation.surface: A critic has little hope for a dreadful movie called Spies.
explanation.definitionFit: A pessimist expects the worst, so is someone holding out little hope.

clue.text: Engineers cut back on explosive and have another look

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: back means turned the other way, so the word for cut is read backwards

parts.note: to axe is to cut
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Army engineers reduce their use of explosives and reconsider.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect or scrutinise something for a second time is to have another look at it.

clue.text: Rector apparently camping at religious council

indicators.note: apparently signals that the rector seems to be within the shelter, so the letter goes inside it

parts.note: someone camping is under canvas, in a tent

explanation.surface: A vicar seems to be sleeping under canvas at a church synod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camping' implies a tent, and 'apparently' puts R inside it. The Council of Trent (1545-63) shaped the Catholic Counter-Reformation.
explanation.definitionFit: Trent was the city that hosted the major sixteenth-century Catholic council, which is named after it.

clue.text: Beat one maturing bird

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them
an ager is something that ages, one maturing

explanation.surface: Thrashing an ageing bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The tanager is a brightly coloured American songbird.

clue.text: Got too old for 4 — we got smashed!

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the numeral spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: Revellers admit they are too old for something, having got drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a reference to another clue, but it is the number spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow out of something is to become too old or big for it.

clue.text: Spy additional line for resistance

indicators.note: one thing for another means in its place, so one letter replaces the other

parts.note: more means additional, extra
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A spy is given an extra line of dialogue in a resistance drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a spy who works inside an organisation for years before betraying it.

clue.text: Let increased uncertainty be heard

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so the phrase is said out loud for the answer

parts.note: increased means higher and uncertainty means doubt

explanation.surface: A command to allow growing doubts to be voiced.
explanation.walkthrough: In the non-rhotic speech of most of England, the R in 'higher' is silent, so HIGHER DOUBT and HIRED OUT sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To let a property or tool is to hire it out to someone for a fee.

clue.text: Academic tempting one to circumvent European court

indicators.note: to circumvent is to go round, so the tempter goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a lurer is someone who tempts

explanation.surface: A seductive professor manages to dodge a European court.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecturer is a university teacher, so a member of the academic staff.

clue.text: Oddly skewers spies

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters, the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: Strangely, the skewers belong to spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spies' is the verb, not a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To spy something is to see it, so 'spies' and the answer are the same verb form.

clue.text: Being given to fleshly pleasures puts non-smoking university in a fix

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside, here within the word for a fix

parts.note: to seal something is to fix it shut; a seal fixes it
NS is the abbreviation for non-smoking

explanation.surface: A hedonist is in trouble because a non-smoking university cramps their style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a fix' reads as trouble, but 'in' is the containment signal and 'a fix' is SEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensual person is devoted to physical, bodily gratification.

clue.text: Delicate dossier about fund- raising at university

indicators.note: about means around, so the dossier goes round the other piece

parts.note: a file is a dossier of documents
in Britain a student rag is an annual charity fund-raising event

explanation.surface: A sensitive dossier about how a university raises money.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG is British student charity fund-raising, with its rag week of stunts and collections.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragile and delicate are synonyms: both mean easily broken or damaged.

clue.text: Poultry farmer's problem is predator eating bird quietly

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the predator holds the other pieces

parts.note: a fox is a predator
an owl is a bird
P, piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: A poultry farmer's trouble: a fox silently devouring a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Fowlpox is a viral disease of chickens and turkeys, a real worry for a poultry keeper.

clue.text: Acid lake busy dissolving American spy

parts.note: a strong acid has a pH of 1, read as PH and I

indicators.note: something dissolving disappears, so those letters vanish from busy

explanation.surface: Acid poured into a busy lake dissolves an American spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Kim Philby was a British intelligence officer and one of the Cambridge Five who spied for the Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Kim Philby is a famous double agent, so an example of a spy.

clue.text: Hidden nearby, a slice of toast

parts.note: close means nearby

indicators.note: a slice is a small piece, here just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Somewhere close by, a slice of toast is tucked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Closet as an adjective means secret or concealed, as in a closet fan.

clue.text: Gloria accepts sovereign's greeting

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the ring of light holds the coin letter

parts.note: a gloria is a halo or ring of light
a sovereign is a gold pound coin, and L stands for pound

explanation.surface: Gloria graciously receives a greeting from the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloria' looks like a name; it is a halo. A sovereign is an old British gold pound coin, and L (libra) is the pound sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallo is a variant of hello, a word of greeting.

clue.text: Replacement spy kidnaps small merchant

indicators.note: a kidnapper holds the victim, so the spy phrase goes round the letter

parts.note: a replacement spy is a new agent

explanation.surface: A substitute spy abducts a small-time trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agent' and 'merchant' both suggest business; the definition is the trader as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsagent is a shopkeeper selling newspapers and magazines, a type of retail merchant.

clue.text: Happened to briefly see Carol naked earlier

indicators.note: earlier means the stripped name comes before the cut-short verb
naked means stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters of Carol go
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of see is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone was pleased to catch a glimpse of Carol undressed beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose means came about or occurred, which is what happened means.

clue.text: Endure president at final judgment

parts.note: to last is to endure
Donald Trump, US president when the puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: Putting up with the president at his day of reckoning.
explanation.definitionFit: The last trump is the trumpet call that announces the Day of Judgment in Christian belief.

clue.text: Smell moving back round to head of river in Portugal

indicators.note: the last letter moves back round to the head of the word, its front

parts.note: the Douro flows through northern Portugal to Porto

explanation.surface: A smell drifts back around towards the source of a Portuguese river.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell, usually an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Still, every memorable event ends

indicators.note: the ends of the words are their final letters, one taken from each

explanation.surface: Even so, every memorable occasion comes to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and yet are synonyms meaning even so, nevertheless.

clue.text: Lift exile ordered by Her Majesty for American spy

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, so the two words are rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen orders an exile to be airlifted, an American spy among them.
explanation.walkthrough: Felix Leiter is the CIA agent who is James Bond's friend in Ian Fleming's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Felix Leiter is Bond's CIA ally, so a fictional spy from the USA.
